sampling_model.design: Two-arm predictable sequential randomization through recruitment time \(T\), with known logged propensities, deterministic lower-envelope quotas, and records observed through the prespecified terminal time \(H_T=T+\Delta_T\).
sampling_model.units: One independent and identically distributed potential outcome-delay vector arrives at each integer recruitment time \(t\leq T\); each revealed assigned response records its calendar revelation time and realized delay.
sampling_model.treatment: The prespecified rare arm satisfies \(\pi_t(1)\geq ct^{-\alpha}\), and the control arm satisfies \(\pi_t(0)\geq\varepsilon\). Policies may allocate the designated arm more often than order \(t^{-\alpha}\). The former two-sided comparability class remains a contained hard subclass because \(ct^{-\alpha}\leq\pi_t(1)\leq Ct^{-\alpha}\) implies the control floor when \(C\leq1-\varepsilon\).
sampling_model.overlap: The headline class uses the one-sided polynomial forced-exploration floor plus the control-arm floor. Lower-envelope quotas give policy-uniform achievability even when \(t^\alpha\pi_t(1)\) does not converge; a single fixed policy \(\pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha}\) inside the class fixes the hard information order for the class-minimax converse.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No delay law or outcome regression is estimated. The procedure uses terminally observable fixed-age indicators, sample variances, a known tail envelope, and an observable variance gate.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their estimator converges to a normal distribution under appropriate conditions.
The observed empirical mean is no longer an unbiased estimator of the expected reward.
They only assume that there is a bound on the tail of the delay.
With bounded or sub-Gaussian reward distributions, the upper bounds are optimal with a matching lower bound.
Maximum likelihood estimators from such a trial have the usual asymptotic properties.
The adaptively-weighted estimator is consistent, and the studentized statistic is asymptotically normal.
Their stabilized estimator is asymptotically normal under consistent conditional-standard-deviation estimation.
They derive finite-sample optimal confidence intervals and sharp efficiency bounds under normal errors with known variance.
Their central limit theorem enables semiparametrically efficient inference at fixed sample sizes.
They derive the efficient influence function under propensities bounded away from zero and one.

body.tldr: Under the published one-sided polynomial exploration regime—\(\pi_t(1)\geq ct^{-\alpha}\) together with a control-arm floor—and allowing the endpoint and its finite delay to be arbitrarily dependent subject to the known envelope \(L(1+u)^{-\beta}\), a measurable two-cohort gate-and-fallback interval for the eventual arm-mean contrast has exact class-minimax expected-length order \(\max\{T^{-(1-\alpha)/2},(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\}\). A fixed admissible policy supplies both matching converse experiments. The ordinary-Wald boundary is the vanishing tail-envelope-to-standard-error ratio, and the bounded-shift Gaussian critical value is attained at the phase boundary.

project_justification.gap: Delayed adaptive-inference theory treats one-sided forced exploration but centers scores using outcome--delay independence; reward-dependent-delay theory supplies regret lower bounds rather than uniformly honest intervals for an eventual causal contrast.
project_justification.niche: The missing design-based object is the exact expected-length frontier under the one-sided exploration allocation regime when logged propensities may oscillate, revelation is informative, and prespecified post-recruitment follow-up changes the observed endpoint set.
project_justification.fill: The project combines an unconditional arm-tape reduction, deterministic shifted two-cohort prefixes, an observable variance gate with a concentration fallback, and same-policy prompt-tilt and hidden-sign experiments to prove the frontier, the ordinary-Wald boundary, and the follow-up elbow.

body.related_work: Shi, Wang, and Wu provide the design-side anchor through a one-sided polynomial forced-exploration condition. The present result uses that allocation regime but extends inference to outcome-dependent delays, so it does not claim to cover their full outcome--delay-independence model as a special case in the converse direction: the hidden-sign tail witness deliberately lies outside that independence subclass. Hadad et al. and Bibaut et al. develop predictable weighting and variance stabilization for prompt outcomes. Manegueu et al. and Vernade et al. motivate polynomial delay-tail control under more restrictive delay structures. Lancewicki et al. and Tang, Wang, and Zheng analyze reward-dependent-delay bias and regret rather than interval length. Bai, Hu, and Rosenberger and Ma, Wang, and Wei obtain classical delayed response-adaptive asymptotics under ignorable-delay conditions. Armstrong and Kolesár provide the bounded-bias Gaussian calibration adapted to the attained boundary here. Liberali et al. are the cardiovascular-trial consumer: their real-time delayed-endpoint intervals need either a tail pad or follow-up sufficient for the uniform boundary, unless a stronger prompt or ignorable-delay law is separately certified.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The order frontier, uniform gate theorem, and attained bounded-shift calibration are proved, but exact normalized expected-length constants and the globally optimal variable-length or randomized interval remain open. The construction intentionally discards assignments beyond deterministic quotas, so it is order-optimal rather than constant-efficient for policies that explore more aggressively. Uniform validity uses a known tail envelope, independent and identically distributed stationary arrival vectors, bounded outcomes, finite delays implied by the polynomial envelope, and a prespecified terminal time; unknown envelope parameters, cross-arrival dependence, and nonstationary endpoint rates are outside scope.
body.honest_scope: The exact minimax order is over the one-sided forced-exploration class with a control-arm floor, not merely over the two-sided comparable-policy subclass. The same fixed policy \(\pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha}\) is used in both lower-bound pairs. The informative hidden-sign converse is not claimed for the outcome--delay-independence subclass of the anchor paper. On regular variance sequences, ordinary Wald is uniformly honest exactly when \(T^q(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\to0\), where \(q=(1-\alpha)/2\). Consequently no follow-up is needed when \(\beta>q\); when \(\beta=q\), one needs \(\Delta_T/T\to\infty\); and when \(\beta<q\), one needs \(T+\Delta_T\gg T^{q/\beta}\). Outside this boundary the bias-aware Gaussian branch or concentration fallback supplies coverage. Application to a particular cardiovascular trial still requires an audit of stationarity, logged propensities, the tail envelope, terminal ascertainment, and the risk-difference estimand.
